title: ATLAS Go: Rehearse Before You Ride — A Digital Twin-Driven Multi-Agent Intelligence Framework for Ride-Hailing and Food Delivery
content: Every minute, a ride-hailing platform decides which driver to send, what to charge, where idle cars should wait and when a courier should leave for a kitchen—while the software platform underneath must itself reshape to the load. We present ATLAS Go, an open ride-hailing and food-delivery system in which each of these decisions is made by an explicit algorithm, rehearsed before it is executed and checked before anyone sees it. The system is organised in four layers on top of an adaptive platform. The platform chooses every five seconds which software modules run inside a monolith and which run as microservices, by solving a binary integer program (BIP) in three phases—perceive; optimise by exact enumeration (2a) or LP relaxation (2b); round, repair and transition—cutting p99 latency from 129.6 ms to 90.0 ms at 22% lower cost than tuned microservices. Layer 1 (learning) runs on the phone: an LSTM forecasts demand, a policy-gradient agent dispatches rides, two Q-learning agents time couriers and add drivers, and an LSTM+RL loop retrains both models every night but keeps a new model only if it beats the old one on held-out data. Layer 2 (agents) is a digital twin of the city in which a dispatch agent and a pricing agent rehearse their decisions 200 times before acting; trained as actor–critic learners with one shared critic (MAPPO), the dispatch agent's learning signal becomes about 40% less noisy. Layer 3 is the Guardian, a runtime shield that blocks any out-of-bounds decision; it caught 3000 of 3000 injected faults with no false alarm. Layer 4 is the phone itself: riders, drivers and kitchens see explained decisions, and whenever Layer 2 fails or is switched off, every screen falls back to Layer 1. We compare the design with Uber, Ola and FREENOW at feature level. All code, data, tests and 44 teaching experiments are public.
